name: Scurceol Hyrde

facts.text: Level 81, 30,000 health, region 61. Four Lyft Miht orbs (level 90, 15,000 health) spawn in the corners of his room and float 450-790 above the floor; while any lives he takes no damage and has 320 Strength instead of 260.
An orb struck by a player may, 8-15 seconds later, hurl that player to a spot on the floor for 20% of their health as falling damage. Dead orbs stay dead through his resets.
Scur means 'shower, storm' (Bosworth-Toller). Ceol 'ship', hyrde 'keeper, shepherd', lyft 'air' and miht 'might' are standard glosses, to verify.
No period player legend found for him.

story:
In the old days Krondon's storm-keeper was called the Scurceol Hyrde, the shepherd of the storm-ship. His craft was weather. When raiders came for Avalon's shore he loosed his storm on them, and when the hall needed calm he held it. To hold a storm still he took four airs out of the sky and bound them in the four corners of his chamber as lights, high up under the roof, and while they burned nothing in the world could wound him and his arm fell like a gale. When Morgana's war came and the thrawn ogres took the hall, the shepherd made his bargain with their queen: his storm for his chamber. He is still down there with the four lights burning. Strike a light carelessly and the bound air flings you across the room like a torn sail. Put all four out and he is only an old man in a cold room, and he knows it.

The last hall-born master. Of all the masters of the old hall, only the Scurceol Hyrde kept his chamber when the ogres came, and he kept it by bargain, not by strength. He knew his craft would be worth more to Orylle than his death, and he offered her his storm for his room. She took it. Since then the squalls off Caldey that wreck the ships of Albion have come from his chamber, and the ogres call him a traitor to the hall behind his back, and the ghosts call him worse.

The four lights. The airs he bound are not his servants. They are prisoners, the four winds of the isles taken out of the sky and set in the corners of his chamber, high under the roof, burning as cold lights. While any of them burns, the bound air wraps him like a gale-coat and no blade bites him, and his arm falls with the weight of a storm. The airs hate him. When a mortal strikes one carelessly, the bound wind lashes out at whatever is nearest and flings it across the room, and the fall breaks bones. Kill a light and it stays dead; the hyrde cannot catch a wind twice. Put all four out and he is only an old man in a cold room, the last keeper of a hall that has forgotten him.
legend:
Put out the four lights in the corners before you touch him. Until then he cannot be hurt and hits like a gale. One party per light, shoot from the floor under it, and mind your footing: a light that throws you does it a few seconds late. A light you kill stays dead even if you wipe on him. Old Avalonians say a sudden squall off Caldey means he is restless.

The lights float high in the corners; ranged fight them from the floor below, melee stand under them and wait. A thrown raider walks back to the same light. Never fight him three thousand units out in the corridors: fight him in his own room, near his spawn, with one tank party holding him while the lights die.

The hall is the queen's. The weather is mine.

The squall passes. It always passes.

lairEntry: Four lights burn in the corners. The air is held still.
The air in this room is held, like a breath.

phases.text: A light goes out. The air in the room stirs.
The lights go out. The storm-keeper can bleed.

loremasterTopic.text: The Scurceol Hyrde, the shepherd of the storm-ship. He bound four airs as lights in his chamber. While they burn, no blade bites him. Tell your raid leader that before you go, not after.

bookPage: The keepers of Krondon did not count wealth in gold but in weather. A hall with a good storm-shepherd kept its shore, and the Hyrde of Krondon was the best of them. I have read that he took the four winds out of the sky and set them in the corners of his chamber, that he might hold a storm still as a man holds a hound. If that is so, the winds are there yet, and they hate him; when we struck the lights, the air threw us about the room as if glad to be asked. When the last went out he sat down. Sailors out of Caldey will not speak his name at sea.
